Nothing shipped, nothing on production changed

No push, no deploy, no write to the production database. Every run used the e2e test database (Neon outreach-e2e, endpoint ep-little-recipe) or a throwaway Vercel Sandbox, deleted afterwards with its snapshots. No email went out: ALERT_EMAIL_TO is empty on the local server, and a unit test fails if any module other than the listed ops ones sends mail.

You consented to testing both plans. Both ran end to end against real TikTok, with writes going only to the test database. The figures below are the runs' own JSON, kept in docs/qa/evidence/. They hold counts only, no handles.

  • Soak 1 found a bad region, and soak 2 confirms the fix. All 59 of soak 1's walls came from cdg1 (Paris): its 4 boots read 111 pages, 52 of them proper, while the four US lanes read 467 of 467. Soak 2 swapped in yul1 (Montreal) and reached 99.5%, with 3 walls (1 on cle1, 2 on yul1) and 0 failures. Lane regions are set through TRACKER_V2_REGIONS.

  • 86 creators were skipped at the 246 s deadline. 671 reads were due and 588 were made, so the rest stay due for the next run. That is the queue working as designed.
  • T3's 13k reads a day is projected. 588 reads per hourly run × 24 ≈ 14.1k a day △, at 5 lanes. No 24-hour soak was run.

Capacity, from the numbers above △: one worker is one address paced at 1.8 s, about 130 reads in a 4-minute hourly run, or about 3.1k a day. Carrying all of today's TikTok load on B would take about 4 workers, or longer runs. B is a standby for now, so one worker is enough to keep it proven.

03The switch drill (T7) ●

scripts/qa/switch-drill.mjs drives the real ops page against the local server:

  1. Failing check. The real daily-check.mjs runs against a deliberately broken worker (wrong token) and scores 0/12. The result is reported to /api/trackers/source-health, and switching to B must then be refused.
  2. Passing check. A real check runs through a fresh Sandbox worker and is reported. The page's own flow then switches to B: Plan B, Review switch, the confirm step, Confirm switch.
  3. Restore. The switch goes back to the position the drill found.

04Alerts and ops guards

Alerts to you only (T8)

  • Measured locally ●: two failing daily checks in a row log "Plan B's daily check failed two days in a row" through alertOps. No email went out, because ALERT_EMAIL_TO is empty here.
  • Not shown: the email reaching your inbox. That needs ALERT_EMAIL_TO set where the cron runs, so the plan's "a test alert reaches you" is still open.
  • A test pins who can send mail. __tests__/unit/lib/noCreatorEmail.test.ts lists every module allowed to send. The new senders all go through alertOps: Plan B health, reader v2 health, the hourly canary, the spend meters and the Sandbox cap. A new sender anywhere else fails the suite.

Ops guards (§13 C and M) ●

  • Kill switches and heartbeats. Every cron is wrapped in cronRoute, which gives it a kill switch and a heartbeat, both stored in the database.
  • Breakers per source. Reader v2 and the post sync each have one.
  • Daily Sandbox cap, 600 by default, enforced through one createSandbox wrapper that also forces persistent:false.
  • Hourly canary. It reads only our own database. Liveness: did every job run when vercel.json says, finish, and finish well; are any switches off or breakers open. Values: are the numbers the jobs wrote plausible, since a cron that runs on time and writes zeros is what a liveness check misses. A problem that lasts all day sends one mail, not 24.
  • Weekly meters. Neon CU-hours through the v2 consumption API, and Sandbox spend from our own counter, since Vercel's usage API answers 404 to a user token. Both alert at 120% of the model.
  • One page, /platform/ops, shows all of it.
  • Before the tables exist, nothing changes. Nothing is killed, no heartbeat is written, and every handler behaves as it does today.

The final run also caught one regression from the age labels: on /creators each roster card's age sat loose inside its <dl>. 08What changes for LKM, branch by branch

Each list comes from the branch's own hand-back, checked against the code where it mattered. Every new table sits behind a ready-guard, so until its table is applied each branch runs the old path.

Creator K-fixes (K1–K3, K5, connect links)

  • Before the DDL, the connect-link API answers 503 and /connect/* says the link is no longer active. Existing flows are unchanged.
  • The 05:00 cron makes up to 200 × (token refresh + profile read) calls a day and overwrites stored profile stats on connected accounts. It skips the write if the token now names a different account.
  • Meta deauthorize and data deletion now really delete Facebook and Instagram-via-Facebook rows, once a grantor id is known.
  • TikTok authorization.removed deletes every row with that open_id, in every org.
  • Connect links have no expiry and are not single-use (a decision for you, section 10).

Lists L-1

  • Once its tables exist: the All tab hides archived lists, and a list rate replaces the roster rate on the share page when price is on.
  • One extra grouped read on the public share page per view while engagement rate is on, which is the default.
  • The decision route's 120/min limit is held in memory, so it applies per server instance.

Creator app (K6, K7, F10)

  • F10 tightens access: a campaign marked invitation-only no longer shows to a creator who merely shares a handle with a roster row.
  • /api/portal/campaigns now returns {joined, invited}; parked portal URLs answer 307 to Home; invite links are /invite/<token>.
  • There is no creator password reset. A signed-out visitor to an invitation-only campaign sees a join error.
  • Covered by the full e2e run in section 7.

Bulk paste and unknown-is-never-0 (F14, A1)

  • Exports gain a "Why a figure is —" column, and unknown figures show as — instead of 0. Average engagement changes wherever a 0 used to be averaged in.
  • A bulk add can take about 90 s longer per link that does not answer. Rows are reconciled, not reported as failed.

Track all (F3)

  • Track all stays shut for LKM until reader v2 runs at 100% with LKM in scope. Elsewhere it allows at most 25 per request, and a single add goes to the back of the queue.
  • About 9.3k lookups per Trackers page view △ (not measured). Bulk needs creators:create. A single add racing a bulk add can exceed the limit by one. There is no bulk untrack.
  • LKM's tracker limit is a separate problem (T-1, section 10).

Colour tokens

  • Light and dark status chips now follow theme colours rather than fixed pastels. CreatorCore changes only where listed in the branch notes (portal indigo → primary, a few public-page tints). Screenshots in section 5.

Ops guards (C, M)

  • Every cron is wrapped. Before the tables exist, nothing changes.
  • The daily read-share alert may fire once a day while the legacy sweep is live, if the 132 h median gap measured on 09-30 still holds ○.
  • A cap refusal counts as a source failure, so the cap can open the TikTok post-reads breaker, which probes again after 2 h.
  • Lanes booting together can overshoot the cap by up to the number of lanes.

Grants (K4, A7/A8)

  • Once CreatorGrant exists, any connection without a grant stops lending its token, and the reader falls back to the public read. Read the backfill dry run first.
  • A failed grant write after a successful connect is only logged, not sent to alertOps.
  • Reader v2 can take a granted connection's follower count as the reading (exit connected). Only orgs on the v2 rollout are affected.
  • Only reader v2 uses the field-source priority so far. The legacy writers were left alone on purpose.

Ages and post status (A2, A4, A5, A6)

  • Every metric export gains trailing columns (As of, Source, Post status). Anything that reads those sheets by position from the right will shift.
  • Unknown export cells are now “—”, not blank. A sheet formula that sums a column will skip them; a script that parses numbers may not.
  • Client-facing share pages and the share PDF gain status wording and a “Data as of” line.
  • The Instagram profile read now asks for id in the same Business Discovery call; one extra upsert per successful read once CreatorPlatformAccountId exists (wrapped, never throws).
  • syncPost keeps since and strikes in its __lastFetch note.

Backups (§13 B)

  • With token B unset, a throttled me/accounts lookup now reads “rate-limited” instead of “not a professional account”. That is a fix, and it is visible on the roster.
  • YouTube changes only when videos.list answers 403 quotaExceeded: then post stats come from batchGetStats, and anything it does not return is “platform refused”, never 0 or deleted.
  • Once enabled, the Plan B VM holds CRON_SECRET, which it never did before. A backup trigger can overlap a late Vercel run of the same job; one trigger per job per 30 minutes is the cap.
  • Nothing of this runs until you set the variables: the route is a 404 and the timer is off.

09Before any of this reaches prod

Order matters. The tables go first, then the code that reads them (F6). Every step below is yours to approve, because LKM prod writes need your rule, not a chat approval.

Tables: 18 new, all additive, none altering an existing table

POST /api/admin/migrate-creator-account-idsCreatorPlatformAccountId (A4). Until it exists the writer does nothing; nothing breaks.
POST /api/admin/migrate-ops-quotaOpsQuotaDay (YouTube batchGetStats quota, §13 B). Kept out of the ops-guard ready check on purpose, so it cannot switch the guards off. Until it exists the fallback still works, its quota is just not counted here.
GET then POST /api/admin/backfill-creator-grants (dry run), then POST /api/admin/migrate-creator-grantsCreatorGrant, with its backfill in the same transaction (K4). Read the dry-run counts first: once the table exists, any connection without a grant stops lending its token.

Run on the final build (6c9a5ff) against the e2e test database, through the real admin routes with the bearer token, in the order above: inspect, apply, apply again, inspect. Every call answered 200. The two tables new tonight went from missing to ready (CreatorPlatformAccountId, OpsQuotaDay), as did CreatorGrant; the four groups already applied stayed ready, and every second apply was a no-op (before and after both ready). The grants dry run counted 0 connections on the test database, so the backfill had nothing to grant there; its rules (manual, dev, unreadable, no identity) are covered by unit tests only. On prod, read the dry-run counts before the apply. Script: scripts/qa/ddl-rehearsal.sh.

The ship itself

This branch holds 10 merged feature branches, plus the work done on it directly (tracker reader, drill, accessibility). The deploy gate will want unit, the full Playwright suite and a build on the exact tree, and prisma/ and globals.css both force the full suite. Ship it as usual: rebase onto origin/master first, then run the suites, then push master, and check with prod-status --expect. Not before you say so.

10Decisions and actions for you

  1. U-1, the brand colour. Dark's last 108 contrast debts all come from one blue. Pick the colour, and I'll split it into separate fill and text tokens under .dark.
  2. T-1, LKM's tracker limit. LKM is on pro, where the limit falls back to 100 trackers, with 1,850+ in use. So every new tracker is refused today (F2), and Track all is held shut for LKM until reader v2 runs at 100%. This needs a plan override on prod, which is a prod write and your call. Run ! neonctl auth first, because the Neon CLI session had expired.
  3. Approve the prod DDL in section 09, in that order, when you want to ship.
  4. Set ALERT_EMAIL_TO to your address in Vercel, so a real test alert can reach you (T8).
  5. Connect-link expiry. How long should an agency's /connect link live? The code sets a value today that you have not confirmed.
  6. Backups, when you want them live. Set INSTAGRAM_BD_TOKEN_B (a second Meta app or Page token) in Vercel. For the backup scheduler, set OPS_SCHEDULER_TOKEN in Vercel and on the Plan B VM, put CRON_SECRET on the VM, then run systemctl enable --now outreach-backup-scheduler.timer yourself. Until then all three behave exactly as today.
  7. Post "Deleted" needs a second strike in the sync cron. The status resolver calls a post deleted only after two checks, but sync-posts settles a post on the first "deleted" answer. In practice a deleted post shows "Unverified" until someone refreshes it. Changing the cron is outside tonight's plan; say if you want it.
  8. Nothing goes to master until you say so.
